body: is this `searched_polygon_count` really the number of plygon that you want to consider, or more an iteration count ? Because if we restart the search if the end is not reachable, then you will re iterate polygons, so this increment may be wrong. If this is more an iteration_cost, then it's ok, but maybe rename it ?
you could square this one too, and have edge_length be length_squared to avoid some square roots. You just need a final square root at the end then (and in the if check_max_length )
maybe uint_32 ? No need to go negative
I mean even with the reset in the current loop we still search those polygons (double) so they count as searched, right? no?

I don't really get what you mean, but my point is when we reset the endpoint, (near line 380) you will restart at the begin_poly, and reset the search. So it will search polygons you already looked at, but you will increase  searched_polygon_count eitherway.
Keeping it int as gdscript cant diff unsigned and this way we can have negative numbers as unlimited instead of wrap which is more user friendly.
Running into subtle distance bugs with this so not changing this for the first iteration.
Could rename it to processed_polygon_count or something because it is the counter to know when to break the path search and return whatever we have at that point.
I would go with `iteration_count` as it is what you're doing. Or maybe just add a comment that the same polygon could be counted multiple times, by design, not an error.
